From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: MAP draft & tech eval milestone (next steps)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the MAP and technical evaluation milestone.

Summary from call:
- Goal: validate latency, cost, and quality for the search summarization workflow for Acme Docs (pilot scope: 100k monthly queries).
- Timeline: target pilot sign-off by mid-July; production decision by end of July.
- Key stakeholders: Jordan (Product), Asha (Infra), Procurement (vendor/contract).

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical Evaluation Plan (attached: Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx)
Milestone details (draft):
- Deliverable: Tech eval report + benchmark results + recommended model/config
- Success criteria: end-to-end P99 latency <= 250 ms for 256-token inference (on target infra), average token cost <= $0.002/token, BLEU/ROUGE-style quality baseline: >= 0.75 F1 on our labelled set (see tech-eval-criteria.md)
- Model shortlist: Llama-2-13B (quantized), MPT-30B-Instruct (8-bit), RedSea-7B-quant (internal eval), open to your shortlist if you prefer other models
- Responsibilities:
  - Acme: provide evaluation dataset (anonymized) and target query mix by 07/02
  - Redwood: run baseline benchmarks, provide config recommendations, deliver benchmark CSV and report by 07/09
- Dependencies: dataset access + short-lived test VPC (or sample logs) from Asha; access to pilot infra (can use Redwood hosted or Acme dedicated pool)
- Target close date for MAP (mutual): 2027-07-15

Can you confirm the dataset delivery date and whether we should run on Redwood-hosted infra or coordinate to use an Acme test VPC? I attached a first-pass MAP workbook with milestones and owners.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick 15-min sync if helpful.
\Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. Asha and I talked offline and we can get an anonymized sample dataset to you by 07/02 (we'll strip PII). We prefer Redwood to run the initial benchmarks on hosted infra to speed things up; if results look promising we can replicate on our VPC.

Couple of asks from our side:
- Please include p99 and p50 latency for both cold and warm cache runs (warm cache is most important for our UX).
- Add tokenization cost and an estimate of end-to-end cost for our expected traffic (100k queries/mo).

I looped in Procurement so they can flag any doc/contract items early. Target MAP close 07/15 works.
\Jordan

Thanks — adding a couple technical notes to the MAP draft:

1) Orchestration / perf knobs to include in evaluation:
- Batch size tuning (auto-batching up to 8 requests)
- KV cache warmup strategy for repeated session flows
- Quantization profiles (q4_0 vs q8_0) and expected memory/latency tradeoffs
- Async streaming vs sync response for UX-sensitive endpoints

2) Benchmark success criteria (proposed final):
- Latency: warm p99 <= 200 ms (target), cold p99 <= 400 ms (acceptable)
- Cost: avg token cost <= $0.0018/token (target), upper bound $0.0025/token
- Quality: evaluation set F1 >= 0.75 and manual spot-check pass rate >= 90%

3) Model shortlist (preference order for eval):
- RedSea-7B-quant (fast, low-cost)
- Llama-2-13B q4_0 (balanced quality)
- MPT-30B-Instruct (higher quality baseline, higher cost)

Next steps I suggest we lock dataset transfer by COB 07/02, Redwood will run baseline hosted runs 07/03-07/08, deliver report 07/09, and we sync for readout 07/11. If Acme wants replicating runs on your VPC we'll prioritize that week of 07/12.

Jordan — confirm dataset delivery and if we should proceed with Redwood-hosted initial runs.
\Camila Reyes
